cues.en: Welcome back.
cues.zh: 歡迎回來。

cues.en: Let's talk about the types of databases that exist.
cues.zh: 來談有哪些資料庫類型。

cues.en: Now, here's the thing.
cues.zh: 先說一件事。

cues.en: The world of databases is extremely complicated.
cues.zh: 資料庫的世界極其複雜。

cues.en: There are so many databases out there, so many new innovations, different databases for different things.
cues.zh: 有非常多資料庫、不斷有新創新，各種資料庫用於不同事情。

cues.en: It's impossible to know all of them.
cues.zh: 不可能全部都懂。

cues.en: So we're just going to do a brief overview of what exists and why we have so many databases.
cues.zh: 所以只簡單概述有哪些類型，以及為什麼會有這麼多資料庫。

cues.en: So let's start off with the first one.
cues.zh: 先從第一個問題開始。

cues.en: Why do we have so many databases?
cues.zh: 為什麼有這麼多資料庫？

cues.en: I mean, look at this little diagram that I found that is a lot.
cues.zh: 看看我找到的這張小圖，數量真多。

cues.en: Well, because we have different needs with data, different databases are good at different things.
cues.zh: 因為對資料有不同需求，各種資料庫擅長不同事情。

cues.en: So there's many different databases because we need them from different solutions.
cues.zh: 所以需要不同解法，也就有不同資料庫。

cues.en: But the first thing we need to talk about when talking about databases is this idea.
cues.zh: 不過談資料庫，首先要說這個概念。

cues.en: There's three main categories of databases.
cues.zh: 有三大類資料庫。

cues.en: Now, remember, databases are just computers.
cues.zh: 記得，講者在這裡把資料庫簡化比喻成電腦。

cues.en: They're computers with a hard drive, essentially, just like your computers is able to store files and have files available any time.
cues.zh: 基本上就是有硬碟的電腦，像你的電腦能儲存檔案，隨時取得。

cues.en: That's what a database is.
cues.zh: 這就是這裡所說的資料庫。

cues.en: Every time you turn off your computer and turn it back on, you expect your files to be there.
cues.zh: 關機再開機，你會期待檔案仍然存在。

cues.en: And a database is that you expect that your data persists.
cues.zh: 資料庫也是如此，會期待資料持久保存。

cues.en: That is the data that you save.
cues.zh: 也就是已儲存的資料，

cues.en: Whether we turn off the computer or turn it back on, it's still going to be there.
cues.zh: 無論關機、重新開機，仍然存在。

cues.en: And then we can access it.
cues.zh: 然後可以存取，

cues.en: We can modify it.
cues.zh: 可以修改。

cues.en: That's the role of a database.
cues.zh: 這就是資料庫的角色。

cues.en: And we have three main types.
cues.zh: 有三種主要類型。

cues.en: One was the original type of database, which was relational database.
cues.zh: 第一，最初的類型，是關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: A relational database is a database like post graphs or my SQL that allow you to use SQL.
cues.zh: 例如 PostgreSQL、MySQL，讓你使用 SQL，

cues.en: To make transactions, that is, to write to the database, to read to the database using the SQL language.
cues.zh: 進行交易，也就是透過 SQL 語言寫入、讀取資料庫。

cues.en: Now, relational databases were all great until around 2000, when initially we just had one database, one master database that held all the information that we needed.
cues.zh: 講者概述，在約 2000 年之前，關聯式資料庫很好用，最初只需要一個主要資料庫，存放所有資訊。

cues.en: But starting in the 2000, we got more and more data, we collected more and more data, and all of a sudden all that information cannot be stored on just one database.
cues.zh: 但從 2000 年代起，收集的資料越來越多，突然發現單一資料庫無法容納所有資訊。

cues.en: So we had an issue we now needed to databases to hold that information.
cues.zh: 所以遇到問題，需要兩個資料庫來儲存。

cues.en: And although I'm simplifying things, the idea was that now because we need distributed databases, that is, we needed more than one database to store all that data.
cues.zh: 雖然這是簡化說法，但意思是需要分散式資料庫，也就是不只一個資料庫儲存資料。

cues.en: Relational databases didn't have the necessary tools to have this idea of multiple databases working together.
cues.zh: 講者說，關聯式資料庫當時缺乏讓多個資料庫協同運作所需的工具。

cues.en: So no SQL databases were born out of that.
cues.zh: 因此誕生了 NoSQL 資料庫。

cues.en: Databases like MongoDB became popular because for the first time it allowed us to do distributed databases.
cues.zh: MongoDB 等資料庫變得流行；講者將它描述為首次讓分散式資料庫成為可能。

cues.en: That is, we can have different machines, ten, 15 machines, all working together as one database.
cues.zh: 可以有不同機器，例如 10 台、15 台，一起當成同一個資料庫運作。

cues.en: Finally, more recently, we have this idea of a new SQL database.
cues.zh: 最後，比較近期出現 NewSQL 資料庫的概念。

cues.en: What does that mean?
cues.zh: 這代表什麼？

cues.en: Well, new SQL databases are still fairly new, but they tried to get the best of both worlds.
cues.zh: 在課程錄製時，NewSQL 還相當新，希望結合兩者優點。

cues.en: You see, relational databases are really, really good for something called acid transactions.
cues.zh: 關聯式資料庫很擅長所謂 ACID 交易。

cues.en: They have some really nice guarantees when we read and write data to make sure that it's always accurate.
cues.zh: 讀寫資料時有很好的保證，確保資料正確。

cues.en: No SQL databases were a little bit more disorganized, but it allows us to store information on distributed
cues.zh: NoSQL 資料庫的組織方式比較鬆散，但能讓我們將資訊儲存在分散式，

cues.en: databases.
cues.zh: 資料庫中。

cues.en: That is, as our data gets bigger and bigger, we can have a no SQL database on different machines so that it scales up with our data.
cues.zh: 資料越來越多時，可以把 NoSQL 資料庫分布在不同機器，隨資料量擴充。

cues.en: New SQL databases like Vault DB or Cockroach DB are trying to have the distributed nature of NoSQL databases
cues.zh: VoltDB、CockroachDB 等 NewSQL，試著保有 NoSQL 的分散式特性，

cues.en: so we can scale up our data, but also have some of the guarantees of relational databases.
cues.zh: 讓資料量能擴充，同時保有關聯式資料庫的一些保證。

cues.en: Now, these new skills are still in the works, but definitely keep an eye on them.
cues.zh: 這些 NewSQL 在課程錄製時仍持續發展，值得留意。

cues.en: Another way to talk about databases is using databases for their own specific needs.
cues.zh: 另一個介紹資料庫的方式，是依照特定用途。

cues.en: For example, there are some data storage or databases that are specifically used for searches.
cues.zh: 例如有些資料儲存系統、資料庫，專門用於搜尋。

cues.en: For example, Elasticsearch or Sola are used as searching databases.
cues.zh: 像 Elasticsearch、Solr，可作為搜尋用途的資料庫。

cues.en: So we put data in there and it allows us to search for things really fast.
cues.zh: 把資料放進去，就能快速搜尋。

cues.en: Then we have things like computational databases, something like Apache Spark that allows us to use
cues.zh: 講者接著把 Apache Spark 這類工具概稱為運算型資料庫，讓我們使用，

cues.en: the data that we have in the database and make computations and calculations on them.
cues.zh: 資料庫裡的資料，進行運算與計算。

cues.en: And we'll get to Apache Spark shortly.
cues.zh: 稍後會談 Apache Spark。

cues.en: Finally, I just want to introduce you these terms that you might hear when it comes to data engineering, OLTP, and.
cues.zh: 最後介紹資料工程常聽到的術語：OLTP 與 OLAP。

cues.en: You can think of OLTP databases as relational databases or SQL databases.
cues.zh: 可以把 OLTP 想成關聯式或 SQL 資料庫，

cues.en: That allows us to make transactions.
cues.zh: 讓我們進行交易。

cues.en: For example, if you have a Web app and that web app has a user that you can store user information,
cues.zh: 例如網路應用程式有使用者，可以儲存使用者資訊，

cues.en: you can upload photos and have that application interact with the database for a user that's OLTP databases.
cues.zh: 上傳照片，讓應用程式與資料庫互動，為使用者提供服務，這就是 OLTP 的用途。

cues.en: An all app database is usually used for analytical purposes.
cues.zh: OLAP 資料庫通常用於分析。

cues.en: Now I'll leave some resources if you want to really dive deep into this topic.
cues.zh: 想深入了解，我會提供一些資源。

cues.en: But as you can see, there's many ways to describe databases.
cues.zh: 可以看到，描述資料庫的方法很多。

cues.en: We have many different types of databases, but at the end of the day, each database is good for its own specific use.
cues.zh: 有很多不同資料庫，但各自都擅長特定用途。

cues.en: If we look back at our diagram, databases are used everywhere.
cues.zh: 回到圖上，資料庫無所不在。

cues.en: For example, these streams, these are usually OLTP databases, like relational databases that collect information.
cues.zh: 例如這些資料流，通常由 OLTP、關聯式資料庫等收集資訊。

cues.en: Let's say a user on a mobile phone updates their username.
cues.zh: 假設手機使用者更新自己的使用者名稱。

cues.en: All that goes to a relational database, an OLTP database, then a data lake.
cues.zh: 會寫進關聯式、OLTP 資料庫，再進入資料湖。

cues.en: Well, a data lake is another database, usually something like Hadoop, which we're going to talk about, and then that data goes into a data warehouse.
cues.zh: 資料湖也是某種資料儲存系統，例如稍後要談的 Hadoop，接著資料再進資料倉儲。

cues.en: All of these things that we see here are essentially databases.
cues.zh: 講者把這裡所有系統，基本上都視為資料庫。

cues.en: We collect information from different streams.
cues.zh: 從不同資料流收集資訊。

cues.en: We have data lakes, which are databases and data warehouses which are databases.
cues.zh: 有資料湖，也有資料倉儲，這裡都歸在資料庫概念下。

cues.en: So for the next couple of videos, knowing what we know about databases and how we have different types
cues.zh: 接下來幾支影片，運用對資料庫及不同類型，

cues.en: of databases, let's try and figure out how this whole picture of a data engineer works.
cues.zh: 的認識，進一步理解資料工程師工作的整體樣貌。
